attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: There is no nonrelativizing theorem extracting a parity sketch, low-rank transcript, or other analyzable normal form from an arbitrary small circuit for H_N^oplus; direct C(H_N^oplus)>N^{1+epsilon} remains unproved.
steps: Kept the polylog query window L=(log N)^d with d>1 so SAT polynomial-size circuits substitute as N^{o(1)} per query and exhaustive lookup is not automatically subthreshold.
Replaced the generated-OR carrier by H_N^oplus, the parity of M=N^q generated SAT labels.
Computed the target transfer C(H_N^oplus)<=C(G_N)+O(M(s(L)+L)+M), yielding N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)} under SAT in SIZE(L^c).

Checked the previous one-sided separator machinery: it decides existential positivity of OR-bags but loses the parity of the number of satisfiable slots, so it cannot certify or refute XOR hardness without extra label information.
Isolated the new leakage normal form: any small feature or affine sketch plus sparse corrections gives an exact subthreshold circuit for H_N^oplus.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The target bridge is valid, but the source lower bound is a major unrestricted circuit lower bound for an explicit P^SAT truth-table carrier. This is not a proof of P != NP or NP notin P/poly until the aggregate XOR carrier lower bound or an equivalent non-natural source certificate is established.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: XOR Carrier Repair

assumptions: Source lower-bound model is unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuits on N input bits.
The lower bound C(H^{oplus}_{N,G})>N^{1+epsilon} holds for infinitely many N.
G_N outputs M length-L SAT encodings and is computable by circuits of size at most N^rho.
The outer XOR tree and fanout are charged in the circuit-size accounting.
definitions: source object: the N-bit carrier H^{oplus}_{N,G}(x)=oplus_{j<=M} SAT(G_{N,j}(x)) with M=N^q and query length L=(log N)^d.
target object: SAT on length-L inputs and the target consequence SAT notin P/poly, hence NP not subset P/poly by completeness.
controlled interface: replace each generated SAT query by one length-L SAT circuit and compute the outer XOR with fan-in M.
target-preserving condition: fixed d,q,rho,epsilon with L=N^{o(1)}, C(G_N)<=N^rho, max{q,rho}<1+epsilon, and no generator advice encoding SAT labels.

equations.label: carrier_definition
equations.valid_when: Valid when G_{N,j} output length-L encodings of SAT instances and the XOR fan-in M is explicitly charged.

equations.label: substitution_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Applies after one size-s(L) SAT circuit is substituted into every generated query without advice depending on x.

equations.label: polylog_transfer
equations.latex: s(L)\le L^c,\ C(G_N)\le N^{\rho}\ \Rightarrow\ C(H^{\oplus}_{N,G})\le N^{\max\{\rho,q\}+o(1)}.
equations.valid_when: Valid when d is fixed, c is fixed, and L=(log N)^d remains N^{o(1)}.

equations.label: target_consequence
equations.valid_when: Requires the lower bound on the source carrier for infinitely many N and the target-preserving threshold gap to be fixed.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If q>=1+epsilon, rho>=1+epsilon, L is not subpolynomial, or G_N leaks SAT truth labels as advice, the bridge is not a valid target-preserving magnification route.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Repaired bridge lemma replacing OR by XOR while preserving the same quantitative target transfer and avoiding one-sided existential separator leakage.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Parity aggregation over polylog-length generated SAT queries gives a valid target-preserving magnification bridge: an i.o. unrestricted circuit lower bound C(H_N^oplus)>N^{1+epsilon} for a target-clean carrier with max{q,rho}<1+epsilon implies SAT notin P/poly, hence NP not subset P/poly. This is route-level only; the source lower bound is unproved.

assumptions: The separator predicates are one-sided for satisfiability on generated formulas.
The transcript records existential hits, not all slot labels.
The generated range contains bags with at least two independently variable SAT labels.
definitions: OR separator transcript: a sound local predicate family that hits at least one satisfiable generated formula in every positive OR-bag and none in negative bags.
XOR carrier transcript requirement: enough information to determine the parity of all SAT labels in the generated bag.
realizability condition: the generator realizes two bags with the same relaxed separator hit pattern and opposite parity of SAT labels.

equations.label: transcript_ambiguity
equations.valid_when: Valid when the generator realizes same-hit positive bags with different numbers of satisfiable slots modulo two.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the separator family actually recovers every slot label or a parity-sufficient sketch, then it becomes a genuine XOR falsifier rather than an OR-only artifact.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quarantines the old OR-specific separator route for the XOR repair; it names exactly why the prior obstruction does not transfer.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Relaxed one-sided bag separators that can certify the OR carrier do not compute the XOR carrier. They are not a valid source lower-bound certificate or upper-bound falsifier for H_N^oplus unless strengthened to a complete per-slot label transcript or parity predictor.

assumptions: Equality tests for exceptional N-bit inputs cost O(N) gates each.
The postprocessor may be arbitrary nonuniform circuitry, so this is a strong leakage audit.
The source lower bound is exact worst-case circuit size, not average-case hardness.
definitions: parity sketch: a circuit A_N:{0,1}^N->{0,1}^t whose output is postprocessed to predict the XOR of generated SAT labels.
patchable error set: the set E_N of N-bit inputs where B_N(A_N(x)) differs from H_N^oplus(x).
subthreshold regime: C(A_N)+C(B_N)+|E_N|N<N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}.

equations.label: sketch_patch_upper
equations.valid_when: Valid when the sketch is correct outside E_N and exceptional inputs are patched by equality gates.

equations.label: subthreshold_falsifier
equations.valid_when: Applies when eta is a fixed positive gap and the circuit model permits nonuniform sparse-error correction.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Finding such an affine, low-rank, or feature-aggregator predictor immediately falsifies the proposed N^{1+epsilon} source lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Defines the new XOR-specific source audit replacing one-sided separator covers: rule out low-dimensional or low-complexity parity transcripts, not just local certificates.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A subthreshold parity sketch is a concrete falsifier for the XOR source lower bound. If a feature circuit A_N and postprocessor B_N predict H_N^oplus with fewer than N^epsilon exceptional N-bit inputs, equality patching gives an exact circuit below N^{1+epsilon}.

control_decision.pivot_test: If XOR admits a subthreshold affine/feature sketch or if lookup becomes subthreshold for the chosen d,q, quarantine the XOR repair.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only after proving C(H_N^oplus)>N^{1+epsilon} i.o. in unrestricted circuits, or after proving a sound nonrelativizing extraction from arbitrary small H_N^oplus circuits to a falsifiable parity-sketch normal form.
control_decision.reason: The OR carrier is trapped by nonrelativizing locality extraction and per-slot direct-sum demagnification. XOR keeps the target transfer q,rho<1+epsilon but changes the leakage object from existential certificates to parity transcripts.

dependency_updates.description: Added XOR generated-SAT carrier with the same N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)} substitution transfer as OR.
One-sided separator certificates are quarantined for XOR because existential hits do not determine parity.
New source audit: rule out subthreshold parity sketches or feature transcripts with sparse patchable error.
The route still needs an unrestricted circuit lower bound for the aggregate carrier, not per-slot SAT hardness.

falsifiers: threshold collapse: max{q,rho}>=1+epsilon destroys the target-preserving gap
polylog lookup collapse when d<=1 and q plus the lookup exponent falls below 1+epsilon
nonuniform leakage from G_N that encodes SAT labels instead of generating target-clean queries
subthreshold affine-sketch or feature-aggregator predictor for H_N^oplus with fewer than N^epsilon patchable errors
complete per-slot promise solver on the generated range of total size below N^{1+epsilon}
natural-proof style source argument that is dense and constructive against N^{1+epsilon} circuits under standard pseudorandomness assumptions

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: If tau and the sketch/postprocessor sizes stay below 1+epsilon with fewer than N^epsilon errors, sparse patching kills the source lower bound. If random-like generators resist all such sketches, the OR separator obstruction is avoided but a direct arbitrary-circuit lower bound is still needed.
held_fixed_controls: q<1+epsilon and rho<1+epsilon so the target bridge stays valid
d>1 so exhaustive SAT lookup on length-L queries is not a subthreshold falsifier
G_N has no SAT-label advice and its circuit cost is charged
the source lower-bound target remains exact C(H_N^oplus)>N^{1+epsilon} infinitely often
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The OR branch is blocked by relativizing one-sided separator extraction. The XOR carrier tests whether that obstruction was an artifact of existential aggregation while preserving the exact SAT-substitution threshold.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: Fix a target-clean generator G_N producing M=N^q SAT instances of length L=(log N)^d with d>1, and study H_N^oplus(x)=oplus_j SAT(G_{N,j}(x)) under unrestricted N-bit circuits.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A non-natural direct lower bound for H_N^oplus, or a nonrelativizing normal-form theorem showing every subthreshold H_N^oplus circuit yields a subthreshold parity sketch with loss below the gap 1+epsilon-max{q,rho}.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: affine sketch dimension tau, where A_N(x) has N^tau output bits and B_N(A_N(x)) attempts to predict the parity of the generated SAT labels.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 52 contributes a concrete repair: XOR aggregation preserves the valid polylog-query magnification threshold while invalidating the OR-specific one-sided separator obstruction. The new source burden is sharper: prove aggregate parity-carrier hardness or rule out subthreshold parity sketches and sparse corrections. This is route-level progress only, with explicit falsifier tests.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: In the ideal random-label model for G_N, count subthreshold affine sketches of size N^alpha and estimate the tau,alpha,error threshold at which a union bound could certify parity-sketch resistance without pretending to prove the actual explicit carrier lower bound.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: There is no valid low-noise upper bound for unrestricted polynomial-size circuits; XOR fanout gives an explicit leakage channel.
steps: Start with a hoped-for lower bound NS_delta(SAT_m)>A_d delta(k log m)^{d-1}.
Using NS_delta(f)<=delta I(f) and the AC0 influence bound, derive SAT_m notin AC0_d[m^k]. This restricted transfer is valid.
Try to replace AC0_d[m^k] by unrestricted SIZE(m^k) using the same high-noise statistic.
The replacement fails: PAR_m has O(m)-size circuits and NS_delta close to 1/2 when delta*m is large.
Try to repair by defining P_{tau,delta}={truth tables with high NS_delta} and requiring usefulness against all SIZE(m^k).
This repair triggers the natural-proof audit because P_{tau,delta} is constructive and large at random-function thresholds.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation separates SAT from a restricted AC0 target only if the SAT-core noise lower bound is proved. It gives no evidence for P != NP, and the unrestricted extension is blocked by the parity falsifier and by naturalness if usefulness is asserted.

assumptions: d and k are fixed constants before m grows.
Noise flips each input coordinate independently with probability delta.
The AC0 target is the standard constant-depth AND/OR/NOT model with arbitrary fan-in and size counted by gates.
The source truth table is total; promise or partial-function escapes require a separate totalization audit.
definitions: source object: the full truth table of an m-bit Boolean function f_m, with SAT_m as the intended unpadded source slice and N=2^m.
target object: unbounded fan-in De Morgan AC0 circuits of fixed depth d and size at most m^k; unrestricted SIZE(m^k) is deliberately not the target.
controlled interface: the statistic NS_delta(f)=Pr[f(x) != f(y)] under independent delta-bit flips, plus the total-influence upper bound for the named target class.

target-preserving condition: the high-noise witness must occur on the same unpadded source slice being separated; grafting an easy parity or padding branch onto an NP-complete carrier is not target-preserving.

equations.label: noise-sensitivity-definition
equations.valid_when: Valid when f is a total Boolean function on m input coordinates and the noise distribution is product Bernoulli.

equations.label: influence-upper-bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when the noisy input is coupled by sequentially flipping the selected coordinates from a uniform starting point.

equations.label: ac0-influence-bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when C is an unbounded fan-in De Morgan circuit of fixed depth d and size S at least two.

equations.label: restricted-transfer-threshold
equations.valid_when: Valid when the same m-bit source function is compared against the fixed-depth size m^k target without padding leakage.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the claimed target is unrestricted SIZE(m^k), the parity falsifier below makes the transfer invalid.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Computes a route-specific quantitative transfer from a weak analytic lower bound to a restricted circuit lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Noise sensitivity gives a valid quantitative bridge only to circuit classes with proved low-noise upper bounds. For fixed depth d and size S=m^k AC0 circuits, NS_delta above A_d delta (k log m)^{d-1} separates the same m-bit function from AC0_d[m^k]. The bridge is not a P-vs-NP bridge.

assumptions: The unrestricted circuit model allows XOR to be implemented by O(m) AND/OR/NOT gates.
delta may depend on m, including delta=c/m or larger.
definitions: source object: PAR_m on m input bits.
target object: unrestricted fan-in-two Boolean circuits of size O(m).
controlled interface: compare NS_delta with the claimed lower-bound threshold.
target-preserving condition: any proposed high-noise-to-size bridge must reject PAR_m, or it is false.

equations.label: parity-noise
equations.valid_when: Valid when each input bit of parity is flipped independently with probability delta before reevaluation.

equations.label: linear-size-parity
equations.valid_when: Valid when unrestricted Boolean circuits are built from fan-in-two AND, OR, and NOT gates.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A proposed P-vs-NP route fails if its threshold accepts PAR_m while claiming usefulness against SIZE(m^k) for k>1.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Supplies a concrete falsifier to any route asserting that large NS_delta implies superlinear or polynomial unrestricted circuit lower bounds.
candidate_lemmas.statement: High noise sensitivity alone cannot certify unrestricted circuit lower bounds. Parity has linear-size Boolean circuits and nearly maximal noise sensitivity at delta*m bounded away from zero.

assumptions: delta has polynomial-bit rational description.
The threshold tau is below the random-function expectation by a concentration margin.
The route claims usefulness against polynomial-size circuits, not only a restricted class.
definitions: source object: truth tables T in {0,1}^N for m-bit Boolean functions.
target object: nonuniform SIZE(m^k), only for the purpose of auditing a claimed usefulness extension.
controlled interface: exact computation of NS_delta(T) from the truth table in polynomial time in N.
target-preserving condition: usefulness must exclude every m^k-size truth table, not merely every AC0 truth table.

equations.label: random-function-expectation
equations.valid_when: Valid when F is a uniformly random truth table and equal noisy pairs are counted as non-disagreements.

equations.label: constructive-property
equations.valid_when: Valid when the full truth table is supplied and delta has polynomially many bits of precision.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the property is large and useful against SIZE(poly), the route must be non-natural or must refute the relevant PRF assumption.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Audits the natural-proof barrier interaction for any attempted extension from AC0 to SIZE(poly).
candidate_lemmas.statement: A high-noise property is poly(N)-constructive from the full truth table. If its threshold is set in the random-function regime and it is also claimed useful against SIZE(m^k), it becomes a natural-proof object rather than a barrier escape.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if a future route cannot localize the statistic to the SAT core or cannot name a target class with a proved low-noise upper bound.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only if it proves a SAT-core NS_delta lower bound above the AC0 threshold while preserving input length, depth, and size parameters.
control_decision.reason: The branch obtained a quantitative restricted-class bridge and a named obstruction to the P-vs-NP extrapolation.

dependency_updates.description: High-NS truth-table properties are poly(N)-constructive and large near the random-function threshold. If claimed useful against SIZE(poly), the route becomes natural rather than an escape.
The AC0 gate is a truth-table analytic statement and has no nonrelativizing feature by itself. It should be treated as restricted-model progress only.
NS_delta(f)>A_d delta(k log m)^{d-1} is a valid transfer to AC0_d[m^k], with no transfer to unrestricted SIZE(m^k).
Parity-branched padded SAT preserves NP-hardness while injecting high noise from an easy slice, so carrier-level noise evidence is quarantined.

falsifiers: PAR_m has linear-size unrestricted circuits and NS_delta(PAR_m)=(1-(1-2delta)^m)/2, falsifying high-noise-to-SIZE lower-bound claims.
A parity-branched NP-complete language can inherit high noise sensitivity from an easy slice while preserving many-one NP-hardness.
If P_{tau,delta} is large and useful against SIZE(poly), it is a valid natural property and collides with PRF-based natural-proof barriers.
Padding can reduce the SAT core's contribution to the global noise statistic while leaving the measured input length and target size threshold inflated.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: At delta_beta=c/r, the parity slice contributes about (1/4)(1-exp(-2c)) to global NS_delta, independent of SAT hardness. Thus high NS of an NP-complete carrier is not a valid P-vs-NP certificate unless the statistic is localized to the SAT core and paired with a target-class upper bound.
held_fixed_controls: The SAT core and its many-one reduction into the b=0 slice remain unchanged.
The unrestricted target SIZE(n^k) and the fixed-depth restricted target AC0_d[n^k] are named separately.
The noise-rate rule is delta_beta=c/r for a fixed constant c, so the parity slice has constant noise contribution.
The added parity branch is computable by O(r) unrestricted Boolean gates.
gedanken_experiment_design.need_decision: Use now as a falsifier probe for noise-sensitivity lower-bound routes.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The branch needs a concrete target-preserving test because high analytic complexity of an NP-complete carrier can be fabricated by easy noisy padding, so abstract noise-hardness language is not enough.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: Define L_beta on inputs (b,phi,u) with |phi|=m and |u|=r=m^beta: L_beta(0,phi,u)=SAT_m(phi) and L_beta(1,phi,u)=PAR_r(u). The map phi -> (0,phi,0^r) preserves many-one NP-hardness, while the b=1 slice is easy and high-noise.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A valid transfer must prove that the measured noise lower bound survives after deleting easy branches and padding, and must provide a low-noise theorem for the exact target class. For unrestricted SIZE(poly), parity shows that certificate cannot exist in this form.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: beta, the exponent controlling the parity-padding length r=m^beta.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 52 converts noise-sensitivity enthusiasm into a precise target gate: NS_delta above A_d delta(k log m)^{d-1} gives a valid AC0_d[m^k] lower bound via total influence, but high noise is useless for unrestricted SIZE because parity is linear-size and maximally noisy. A parity-branched NP-complete carrier is the concrete falsifier for non-target-preserving noise routes.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Audit whether any non-natural SAT-specific proof can lower-bound NS_delta(SAT_m) at delta=(log m)^{-d} above the AC0 threshold without using a full-truth-table large property useful against SIZE(poly).

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The positive source theorem is missing: we need an E-uniform, no-advice, low-D carrier with a hard row and a certificate excluding every easy-rooted low-volume edit explanation, without simply assuming the desired circuit lower bound.
steps: Fix length m, image entropy D, MCSP threshold s_m=2^{epsilon m}, and an easy anchor A with circuit exponent a.
Assume a candidate selector exposes a root-to-row edit graph with path length exponent eta and edge edit exponent beta.
For a fixed emitted row T_v, hardwire the root circuit and all edited coordinates along one path; compute T_v(x)=A(x) xor the parity of equality tests hitting x.
If max(a,eta+beta)<epsilon, the row cannot be a no-side MCSP witness; for canonical rank traversal eta<=D, the falsifier condition is D+beta<epsilon.
Applying the existing carrier extraction after this audit still gives only the conditional route-level consequence delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)).
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation proves an obstruction to a class of explicit MCSP sources and preserves a conditional extraction theorem. It constructs no hard row and gives no direct proof of P != NP.

assumptions: m is the truth-table input length, N=2^m is the table length, and all circuit bounds are unrestricted Boolean circuit size.
The edit path may be used nonuniformly for a fixed emitted row; hardwiring changed coordinates is allowed in the upper-bound circuit.
The carrier claims MCSP no-side threshold s_m=2^{epsilon m} for at least one emitted row, or for all rows in the stronger universal version.
The extraction theorem uses the existence of one hard row; it does not assert P != NP.
definitions: source object: E-uniform canonical low-image MCSP carrier I_m subset {0,1}^{2^m}, |I_m|<=2^{D m+O(1)}, with an alleged row of unrestricted circuit complexity greater than 2^{epsilon m}.
target object: E language obtained by row-index multiplexing the emitted truth tables and then applying kappa-density padding to all target input lengths.
controlled interface: map a hard row T_{m,j} to L(j,x,pad)=T_{m,j}(x), with row index length Dm+O(1), E-uniform unranking, and no nonuniform length advice.

target-preserving condition: row hardness is against unrestricted nonuniform circuits, the source unranking is E-uniform, padding loses only factor kappa, and no easy-rooted low-volume edit certificate undercuts the MCSP threshold.
easy-rooted edit graph: a graph whose root A has circuits C(A)<=2^{a m+o(m)} and whose edge e changes p_e truth-table positions.
path-volume exponent: every relevant root-to-row path has at most 2^{eta m+O(1)} edges and each edge changes at most 2^{beta m+O(1)} positions.

equations.label: image_entropy
equations.valid_when: Valid when the source lower-bound model is unrestricted nonuniform circuits and distinct emitted truth tables are canonically quotient-counted.

equations.label: path_volume
equations.valid_when: Applies when every path has at most 2^{eta m+O(1)} edges and each edge flips at most 2^{beta m+O(1)} table positions.

equations.label: edit_circuit_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when the root table A has circuits of size 2^{a m+o(m)} and edited coordinates may be hardwired in a nonuniform circuit.

equations.label: rooted_falsifier_threshold
equations.valid_when: Requires the asserted MCSP no-side threshold to be 2^{epsilon m} against unrestricted circuits for the same truth-table length.

equations.label: rank_walk_corollary
equations.latex: D+\beta<\epsilon \Rightarrow \text{rank-walk carrier from an easy endpoint is invalid}
equations.valid_when: Applies when canonical rank traversal visits at most 2^{D m+O(1)} rows and each adjacent update has exponent beta.

equations.label: target_transfer
equations.valid_when: Applies after the reduction preserves E-uniform unranking, kappa-dense padding, and row-index length Dm+O(1).

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Exhibit an easy root, such as zero, parity, or a known PRG row, plus an edit arborescence covering the accepted image with max(a,eta+beta)<epsilon; that makes the source invalid even if random rows with the same D would be combinatorially robust.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Route-specific falsifier and bridge guard: it certifies when an explicit low-D MCSP source collapses to small circuits before the carrier-to-E extraction can be used.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Rooted edit leakage lemma for low-image MCSP carriers: if every emitted table is reachable from a subthreshold easy anchor by paths of cumulative edit exponent below epsilon, then the alleged MCSP no-side source is invalid. For a rank-walk image of entropy D with adjacent update exponent beta, beta+D<epsilon is a concrete falsifier.

assumptions: Circuit upper bounds propagate from a known circuit for one endpoint plus a hardwired edit list.
No known circuit for the endpoint means the propagation inequality is not a subthreshold upper bound.
definitions: source object: low-D image family with an edit graph whose connected components need not contain a known easy table.
target object: the same row-index multiplexed E language used by the MCSP carrier transfer.
controlled interface: only an actual unrestricted hard row transfers; a smooth path without an easy root supplies no target-preserving upper bound.
target-preserving condition: distinguish rooted easy edit paths from unrooted edit geometry, so the route does not quarantine valid hard-anchor constructions.

equations.label: relative_edit_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when the path edits from T_u to T_v are fixed and may be hardwired for the target row.

equations.label: hard_anchor_nonimplication
equations.valid_when: Valid when the only available anchor is potentially hard and no independent small circuit for it is known.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a proposed objection cites smooth traversal but cannot name a subthreshold anchor and path-volume bound, the objection is not a valid falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Prevents an overstrong rank-jump no-go; only easy-rooted low-volume paths are rejected.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Unrooted smooth traversal is not itself a falsifier. Edit closeness between hard-looking rows gives an upper bound only relative to an anchor circuit; if the anchor may already be hard, the inequality does not refute MCSP no-side soundness.

assumptions: The number of generated distinct rows is at most 2^{D m+O(1)}.
The root has circuit exponent a<epsilon.
The claimed hard row lies on a generated prefix from the root.
definitions: source object: E-uniform iterative selector that outputs a low-image family by successive point edits from an easy anchor.
target object: a hard-row multiplexed E language, available only if a generated row truly exceeds the MCSP threshold.
controlled interface: hardwire the prefix edit transcript to convert low-volume generation into a nonuniform circuit for the generated row.
target-preserving condition: the selector must either use a hard anchor, make a large rooted jump, or prove that no low-volume edit transcript reaches the hard row.

equations.label: necessary_jump
equations.valid_when: Valid when at most 2^{D m+O(1)} sequential updates from a subthreshold root are used before reaching the asserted hard row.

equations.label: large_jump_not_sufficient
equations.valid_when: Valid because a large edit is only a necessary anti-leakage condition and does not by itself prove unrestricted circuit lower bounds.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A lexicographic or local-search derandomization of random robust carriers fails if its repair transcript changes only 2^{beta m} positions per row with beta<epsilon-D.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quantitative design rule for explicit non-natural selectors: small incremental repairs are disallowed, but large jumps still need independent soundness.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Iterative repair selectors from an easy table require a macroscopic jump. If M<=2^{D m+O(1)} rows are generated from an easy root and some row is MCSP-hard at threshold 2^{epsilon m}, then at least one update on a root-to-hard prefix must flip about 2^{(epsilon-D)m}/m positions unless the path length exponent exceeds D.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot or quarantine if every candidate low-D source either has a subthreshold easy-rooted edit transcript or can exclude such transcripts only by assuming the desired unrestricted circuit lower bound.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if we construct a no-advice, E-uniform, low-D, cap-compatible source with an actual hard row and a non-natural rooted-volume certificate, yielding delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)).
control_decision.reason: The branch made a contribution-making move by proving a quantitative falsifier for easy-rooted explicit selectors while preserving the conditional E lower-bound bridge.

dependency_updates.description: A low-D carrier must now be audited for easy-rooted edit volume. Soundness at threshold 2^{epsilon m} requires every hard row to evade all root-to-row edit explanations with exponent below epsilon.
The row-index multiplexing transfer remains valid with exponent delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)) once an actual unrestricted hard row and E-uniform unranking are supplied.
E-uniformity is not enough; the explicit construction must not expose a low-volume rooted edit transcript, subthreshold interval decoder, or nonuniform length selector.
The sparse low-D image is not large, so the immediate natural-proofs barrier is avoided; dense constructive postfilters or outside-U repairs remain quarantined as invalid.
Future source proposals must either provide a hard anchor, a large-jump construction, or a proof that no easy-rooted low-volume path reaches the asserted MCSP-hard row.

falsifiers: Rooted edit falsifier: an easy anchor plus a covering arborescence with max(a,eta+beta)<epsilon gives small circuits for every covered row.
Rank-walk falsifier: low-image entropy D and adjacent update exponent beta with D+beta<epsilon invalidate an easy-endpoint iterative carrier.
Interval-decoder falsifier: indexed block restart or ranked random access below exponent epsilon gives a direct circuit upper bound for emitted tables.
Sparse-correction falsifier: accepted rows within O(2^{epsilon m}/m) edits of any subthreshold circuit are not valid MCSP no-side witnesses.
Aggregate-shortcut falsifier: unrestricted aggregate row-forcing below q_force=(D+epsilon)/(1+D) cannot certify an MCSP-hard row.
